title: Norm-attaining residue evaluations on a finite reduced Tate model
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, and let $n\ge0$. Put $T=k\langle X_1,\ldots,X_nangle$, the ring of restricted series [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with Gauss norm $G(\sum a_
u X^
u)=\sup_
u|a_
u|$, and put $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$ with $|f/g|_Q=G(f)/G(g)$. Let $T\hookrightarrow A$ be an injective homomorphism of commutative unital $k$-algebras such that $A$ is a finite $T$-module, reduced (no nonzero nilpotent), and torsion-free over $T$ (multiplication by each nonzero $t\in T$ is injective). Put $M=(T\setminus\{0\})^{-1}A$. For $z\in M$ let $p_z(Z)=Z^r+\sum_{i=1}^r a_iZ^{r-i}$ be its monic annihilating polynomial of least positive degree over $Q$, and set $\sigma(z)=\max_{1\le i\le r}|a_i|_Q^{1/i}$. For every $0
e a\in A$, there exist a finite field extension $k_a/k$ and a unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $\chi_a:A	o k_a$ such that, for the spectral norm $s_{k_a/k}$ [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], $$s_{k_a/k}(\chi_a(b))\le\sigma(b)\quad(b\in A),\qquad s_{k_a/k}(\chi_a(a))=\sigma(a)>0.$$ Stability of $k$, normality of $A$, a domain hypothesis on $A$, and separability are not assumed.

proof.text: The injection $T\hookrightarrow A$ implies $A\ne0$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-algebra-affinoid-presentation] to the identity presentation of $T$ and the finite $T$-algebra $A$. Thus $A$ has an affinoid quotient presentation. By [lem-trf-tate-gauss-multiplicative], $G$ is multiplicative. A nonzero series has a nonzero coefficient, so its Gauss norm is positive; hence $T$ is a domain, and $G(f)/G(g)$ is a well-defined absolute value on $Q$. Torsion-freeness makes $A\to M$ injective: $b/1=0$ implies $tb=0$ for some $t\ne0$, hence $b=0$. These facts justify the fraction-field and localization notation of the statement.

proof.text: For each $b\in A$, apply [lem-trf-tate-torsionfree-fibre-polynomial] to obtain the monic generator $P_b(Z)=Z^r+\sum_{i=1}^r t_iZ^{r-i}$ of the evaluation kernel $T[Z]\to A$. It is also the monic least-degree annihilator of $b/1$ over $Q$. Indeed it annihilates there. If a nonzero $H\in Q[Z]$ of degree less than $r$ annihilated $b/1$, multiply its finitely many coefficients by a common nonzero denominator $t\in T$. Then $tH\in T[Z]$ is nonzero of the same degree, and $(tH)(b)$ maps to zero in $M$. Step 1 makes it zero in $A$, contrary to kernel $(P_b)$, since every nonzero multiple of a monic degree-$r$ polynomial over a domain has degree at least $r$. Monic division over $Q$ also proves uniqueness. Consequently $p_b=P_b$ in $Q[Z]$ and $\sigma(b)=\max_iG(t_i)^{1/i}$. For every maximal $\mathfrak m\subset T$, the same cited theorem gives a finite nonempty fibre $Y_{\mathfrak m}$ and $\max_{\mathfrak n\in Y_{\mathfrak m}}|b\bmod\mathfrak n|=\max_i|t_i\bmod\mathfrak m|^{1/i}$.

proof.text: Every residue field of $A$ or $T$ is finite over $k$ and has a unique extending absolute value by [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. By [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension], the minimal-polynomial spectral norm on any of these finite extensions is a multiplicative extending absolute value; hence uniqueness identifies it with the residue absolute value. Given $\mathfrak n\in\operatorname{Max}A$, its contraction $\mathfrak m$ to $T$ is maximal: $T/\mathfrak m$ injects into the finite-dimensional $k$-field $A/\mathfrak n$, so it is a finite-dimensional domain and therefore a field (multiplication by any nonzero element is an injective, hence surjective, linear map). Apply step 2 to $b$ and this $\mathfrak m$. The cited calculus says $\rho_T=G$, so $|t_i\bmod\mathfrak m|\le G(t_i)$. Thus for every $b\in A$ and every maximal $\mathfrak n$ one has $s_{(A/\mathfrak n)/k}(b\bmod\mathfrak n)\le\sigma(b)$.

proof.text: Fix $0\ne a\in A$. If $\sigma(a)=0$, step 2 makes every coefficient $t_i$ of $P_a$ zero, since $G$ is definite. Then $P_a=Z^r$ and $a^r=0$ with $r\ge1$, contradicting reducedness. Thus $\sigma(a)>0$. Choose an index $i$ attaining the finite maximum in step 2 and put $f=t_i$. Then $G(f)^{1/i}=\sigma(a)>0$, so $f\ne0$.

proof.text: We construct a maximal $\mathfrak m\subset T$ with $|f\bmod\mathfrak m|=G(f)$. Since the coefficients of $f$ tend to zero, one coefficient $c\ne0$ attains $G(f)$: choose any positive coefficient value $v$, take the finite nonempty set of coefficients of value at least $v/2$, and maximize on it; all remaining values are smaller. Put $g=c^{-1}f$, so $G(g)=1$. In $T'=k\langle X_1,\ldots,X_n,Y\rangle$, put $h=1-Yg$. Its constant coefficient is $1$ and $G(h-1)=1$. Therefore [lem-trf-tate-unit-coefficient-criterion] makes $h$ a nonunit. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal], choose a maximal $\mathfrak M\subset T'$ containing $(h)$. The field $L=T'/\mathfrak M$ is finite over $k$, complete, and has coordinate residues $(x_1,\ldots,x_n,y)$ of absolute value at most $1$, by [lem-per-tate-maximal-residue-evaluation]. The restriction $e:T\to L$ of the quotient is the convergent substitution at $x$, by that node's formula for every series; [lem-per-tate-banach-substitution] gives $|e(g)|\le1$. Since $h$ vanishes, $y e(g)=1$, whence $|e(g)|=1$ and $|e(f)|=|c|=G(f)$. The image of $e$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-domain, hence a field by the multiplication argument of step 3. Thus $\mathfrak m=\ker e$ is maximal, and uniqueness of the extending residue absolute value in [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus] identifies $|f\bmod\mathfrak m|$ with $|e(f)|$. This includes $n=0$.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-tate-torsionfree-fibre-polynomial] for $a$ at the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of step 5. Its finite nonempty fibre has an element $\mathfrak n$ attaining $\max_{\mathfrak q\in Y_{\mathfrak m}}|a\bmod\mathfrak q|=\max_j|t_j\bmod\mathfrak m|^{1/j}$. The right side is at least $|t_i\bmod\mathfrak m|^{1/i}=G(t_i)^{1/i}=\sigma(a)$, and step 3 bounds every fibre value by $\sigma(a)$. Hence $|a\bmod\mathfrak n|=\sigma(a)>0$. Set $k_a=A/\mathfrak n$ and let $\chi_a$ be the quotient $k$-algebra homomorphism. It is unital; its target is a finite field extension by [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. Step 3 identifies its residue absolute value with $s_{k_a/k}$ and proves contractivity for every $b\in A$, while the equality just obtained gives the required attainment. No field structure on $M$, normality of $A$, stability, or separability was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NQ-37ccc09aa (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. Its statement is unchanged and true. Tested: n=0 with A=k×k (a=(0,1), and contractivity for b=(x,y)); A=T[Z]/(Z^2-X); an inseparable residue field; a nilpotent a, which shows reducedness is needed. The delivery adds no new nodes, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Step 1: the finite-algebra-affinoid-presentation node applies with base T (identity presentation) and B=A, and B≠0 because T↪A. Gauss-multiplicativity makes T a domain and |·|_Q well defined, and torsion-freeness makes A→M injective. Step 2: the torsion-free fibre-polynomial hypotheses all hold. Clearing denominators correctly shows that its monic P_b is the least-degree polynomial over Q, so σ(b)=max G(t_i)^{1/i}. Step 3: the calculus node gives finite residue fields with a unique extending absolute value and ρ_T=G. The algebraic-extension Mathlib leaf (F=k) makes s that same absolute value; its index form agrees with lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm under i=d-j. The contraction of a maximal ideal is maximal, which gives contractivity. Step 4 (σ(a)>0 from reducedness) is elementary and correct. Step 5 builds h=1-Yg, which is a nonunit by the unit-coefficient criterion (|c_0|=1 is not >1); a maximal ideal containing h exists; residue evaluation and Banach substitution (B=L, |x_i|≤1) give |e(g)|≤1; and y·e(g)=1 gives equality. This repeats the 1-Yg argument from inside the calculus node's proof, but that node's statement gives only the supremum, not attainment, so this is not a C3 use of another node's proof. Step 6 gives attainment on the finite fibre. The three off-unit tool uses (per-tate maximal residue, per-tate Banach substitution, pbc maximal ideal) are the same ones already accepted for the same-unit calculus node; I accept them. Searches for duplicates ('maximum principle', 'attain', 1-Yg) found none. BGR and Bosch are absent locally; WANTED is recorded and the proof is correctly marked agent. No SGA. No fixes.
